body:
## Problem

- API clients that list insights without an `order` param wait tens of seconds per page, and each request pins a web worker for that whole time.
- `order_queryset` fell back to `order_by("order")`. `Insight.order` is a vestigial nullable integer with no index, so Postgres scanned and sorted every insight in the project.
- Offset pagination repeats that scan and sort for every page, so a paginating client pays it again and again.
- The cost lands on the shared production primary, not only on the caller.

- Insight showing the difference in response time https://us.posthog.com/project/2/insights/6MNPaiNR

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d1dc-3d6a-7b10-91a4-aa5ba59bcda2 -->
## Origin

- pganalyze
- First signal: 2026-09-24
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0d1dc-3d6a-7b10-91a4-aa5ba59bcda2)
- Likely cause: [`a6b8e54`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/a6b8e54145c1b11070eddf0acde5a04b7f94ad70)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d1dc-3d6a-7b10-91a4-aa5ba59bcda2 -->

## Changes

- The no-`order` default now sorts on `-last_modified_at`, which the partial index `dashboarditem_team_lmod_idx` on `(team_id, -last_modified_at) WHERE NOT deleted` already covers, so the sort can seek instead of scan.
- The response order changes for unordered list requests: newest-modified first, instead of the arbitrary order a column of NULLs produces. The app's own list views already send `order=-last_modified_at`, so they see no change.
- A small number of API clients call this endpoint with no `order` param.
- Some of those clients have `Insight.order` set on their insights, so their response order changes too.
- This is not zero risk. Affected customers will be contacted before this ships.
- Pagination becomes deterministic. `stable_queryset_ordering` appends `-pk`, so the final sort is `(-last_modified_at, -id)`; the old `(order, id)` sort put every row in one NULL group.

```diff
- ORDER BY "posthog_dashboarditem"."order" ASC, "posthog_dashboarditem"."id" ASC
+ ORDER BY "posthog_dashboarditem"."last_modified_at" DESC, "posthog_dashboarditem"."id" DESC
```

- Mechanical: one query snapshot in `test_insight.ambr` updated to the new `ORDER BY`.
- Not changed: `with_last_viewed_at` still annotates the correlated subquery, because both list serializers expose `last_viewed_at`. With an index-ordered scan the `LIMIT` stops the subplan after one page of rows, so it no longer runs for the whole project.

## How did you test this code?

- Added `test_list_without_order_sorts_by_last_modified_at_descending`. It gives the older insight the lower `order` value, so it fails under the old default and passes under the new one — verified both ways locally. No existing test asserted the default list order.
- Ran `products/product_analytics/backend/tests/api/test_insight.py` locally against the dev stack.
- Not checked: no production `EXPLAIN` was run, so the index seek is inferred from the index definition, not measured.

- Considered and rejected: adding a new index for `(team_id, order)`. The column is vestigial and holds NULL for practically every row, so indexing it would pay storage for an order nobody asked for.
- Considered and rejected: dropping the `with_last_viewed_at` annotation for unordered requests. Both list serializers return `last_viewed_at`, so removing it would change the API response.
